text:
anya: Flagging a weird regression on the reranker int8 bring-up. ndcg@10 down ~2.6% on the docs-harvest sample. not sure if this is quant instability or data-shaped.
sam: can you paste the quick numbers and eval command?
anya: fp16 -> ndcg@10=0.498, mrr=0.379. int8 -> ndcg@10=0.486, mrr=0.374. sample=12k. run like:
```
python -m eval.rerank --model reranker-1.4-fp16 --queries dh_val_12k.jsonl --candidates dh_candidates.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 5
python -m eval.rerank --model reranker-1.4-int8 --queries dh_val_12k.jsonl --candidates dh_candidates.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 5
```
rik: small delta but reproducible? also check that the candidate file wasn't rewritten by the scraper with extra HTML.
anya: good point. I diffed a random 500 docs and found ~3% contain <pre> code blocks and inline math ($...$).
sam: code blocks blow up tokenization; also math symbols can change BPE splits. try a quick canonicalize pass (strip code fences, replace math with placeholder).
anya: ran canonicalize -> int8 ndcg@10=0.495, mrr=0.377. almost recovered.
rik: that's telling: preprocessing mismatch between training/serve and eval is the likely root cause, not quantization.
sam: add rule to candidate scraper: remove code fences and collapse repeated whitespace. add an eval variant that keeps raw html for monitoring.
anya: logging it in the bring-up checklist under "candidate surface parity" and adding a small unit test that checks token-count delta after canonicalization. link: https://internal.gist/canonicalize-dh.py
eval-bot: job 52380 queued: int8 + canonicalize on 100k sample, seeds [5,13]. ETA ~2h.
anya: thanks — will follow up with AB on holdout when jobs finish.
